consistency.note: Three measures, each covering something the others do not. service_stability (no judge) = Jaccard overlap of the services (by URL) each plan recommends, averaged over pairs of plans; the range is the lowest and highest pair. LLM-judged, mean of N repeats with the lowest and highest repeat in *_range: fact_consistency = share of services in two or more plans whose facts (cost, department, deadline, requirements and so on) the judge finds no contradiction in; structure_consistency = share of pairs of plans with the same steps, in the same order, and the same plan summary (the judge lists no differences; which services the steps contain is not compared). Evidence: services_not_in_every_plan, fact_checks (each contradiction with plan numbers) and pairs (each pair's listed differences). Fewer plans give noisier scores. Aggregate = mean of per-profile scores. Plan and repeat numbers are 1-based. weighted_aggregate = per-profile scores averaged with each profile's weight, over the profiles that have a score; coverage.weight_scored is the share of total weight on profiles with plans, out of all weight including profiles skipped for being below --min-weight.

fact_checks.name: Register the birth
fact_checks.rationale: I compared cost, department, deadline, method, location and requirements across the three plans. All give £0, GRO, in-person registration within 42 days, and the register office or hospital. The differences in listed documents and extra detail are compatible.

fact_checks.name: Child Benefit
fact_checks.rationale: I compared cost, department, application methods, the 3-month backdating limit, payment frequency, the £60,000 High Income Child Benefit Charge threshold, the 48-hour wait after registration, and the requirements. The plans agree on all of these, and the differences are only in how much detail each gives (for example, only Plans 1 and 3 list bank details).

fact_checks.name: Statutory Maternity Pay
fact_checks.rationale: I compared the department, cost, eligibility rules (26 weeks' continuous employment by the 15th week before the due date, average earnings of at least £129), the 39-week duration, and the contact methods. All three plans agree. The differences are omissions, such as the MATB1 form appearing only in Plan 2, and different lists of methods, and none of the plans says any method is unavailable.

fact_checks.name: Statutory Paternity Pay
fact_checks.rationale: I compared costs, department, the 52-week deadline, the 26-weeks employment and £129 earnings rules, notice periods, how the leave can be split, and the application methods across the three plans. All agree on these or differ only in how much detail they give.

fact_checks.name: Shared Parental Leave & Pay
fact_checks.rationale: I compared cost, department, methods, eligibility requirements and process across both plans. Both say the service is free, run by HMRC and used online, and both require the mother to end maternity leave/pay early and both parents to meet employment and earnings tests. Plan 1 also mentions eligibility for Statutory Maternity Pay or Maternity Allowance, which Plan 2 omits but does not contradict.

fact_checks.name: Maternity exemption certificate
fact_checks.rationale: I compared cost, department, application methods, requirements, validity period, delivery timing and backdating across both plans. They match: both give 12 months after the birth, 10 working days by post, one month backdating, and midwife, GP or health visitor involvement. The differences are only wording or extra detail.

The plans differ only in how much detail they give, and none of their claims conflict.

All three plans agree on these. Plan 1 does not say both parents must work, but that is an omission, not a conflict.

fact_checks.name: Free childcare — 30 hours (working parents)
fact_checks.rationale: I compared cost, department, application method, eligibility rules (16 hours at minimum wage, £100,000 cap), the 23-week application point, the 9-month start and the 3-monthly reconfirmation. All of these agree or one plan simply adds detail, such as Plan 3 naming the Local Authority alongside HMRC.

fact_checks.name: Free childcare — 15 hours (3 and 4-year-olds)
fact_checks.rationale: I compared eligibility, start timing, hours, cost, department and end point. Both plans say the free hours start the term after the third birthday, are free, are run by the local authority, and stop at reception. Plan 1's 'regardless of work status' applies to the universal 15 hours, so it is compatible with Plan 2's extra hours for working parents.

fact_checks.name: Register the birth
fact_checks.rationale: I compared cost, department, deadline, methods, requirements, location and process across the three plans. fact_checks.name: Child Benefit
fact_checks.rationale: I compared cost, department, application methods, backdating limit, deadline wording, requirements, the £60,000 High Income Child Benefit Charge threshold and payment frequency across the three plans. fact_checks.name: Statutory Paternity Pay

relevance.note: Custom Bedrock judge. A task is 'relevant', 'contradicted' (a fact about the person rules it out) or 'irrelevant'. A plan's score for one repeat = fraction of its tasks judged 'relevant'. scores_by_plan is each plan's score meaned over the N repeats, in plan order; per-profile score = mean of scores_by_plan (plans with no scoreable result are left out); min and max are the lowest and highest plan scores, showing how much a profile's plans differ; repeat_range is the min/max of the profile's score across the N judge repeats. Aggregate = mean of per-profile scores (not a pooled task ratio). Each task lists its verdict and the judge's rationale; repeat and plan numbers are 1-based. weighted_aggregate = per-profile scores averaged with each profile's weight, over the profiles that have a score; coverage.weight_scored is the share of total weight on profiles with plans, out of all weight including profiles skipped for being below --min-weight.
